tip: 'Por' = through/along: 'Caminamos por el parque.' Use 'por' for movement through or past a place.
Double negatives are correct Spanish! 'No le digas nada' = don't tell him NOTHING. After 'no', everything else goes negative too – 'nada', 'nunca', 'nadie'.
'Me encantó' flips the sentence: the FOOD did the enchanting, to me. Like 'gustar', 'encantar' makes the thing you love the subject – you're just the target.
'Hubo' = preterite of 'haber' (there was/were). Singular form even for plurals.
'Ya' means already – but 'ya no' flips to 'not anymore.' 'Ya no existe' = it no longer exists, not 'it already doesn't exist.'
Literally 'they gave him cat for hare' – medieval inns passed off cat as hare meat. 'Dar gato por liebre' = rip someone off with a fake.
'Billete' is both ticket AND banknote. 'Un billete de cincuenta' = a fifty-euro bill – context (and the number) tells you which one you found.
'Aunque' + indicative = although (known fact): 'Aunque llueve, salgo.' Compare: 'aunque' + subjunctive = even if (hypothetical).
'Tocó la puerta' – nobody touched the door. 'Tocar' covers touch, play music, and KNOCK. At a door, 'tocar' means someone's knocking.
'Habrán sido las tres' – future tense about the past?! Spanish uses future for guessing: 'it will have been three' = it must have been around three.
'El agua'... but 'fría'? 'Agua' is feminine – it borrows 'el' only because the stressed a- start would clash with 'la'. Adjectives stay feminine: 'el agua está fría'.
Imperfect ('esperaba') for ongoing wait + preterite ('vi') for the sudden encounter.
Spaniards don't 'take' photos – they MAKE them, on themselves: 'nos hicimos una foto' = we made ourselves a photo. 'Tomar una foto' reads Latin American.
Imperfect ('cocinaba') for ongoing background + preterite ('puso') for completed action.
'Plantado' = planted. 'Me dejó plantado' = he stood me up – literally 'he left me planted', stuck waiting where you stood.
'Por la cual' = for which (formal): 'La razón por la cual...' More literary than 'por la que' but same meaning.
'Solía' is the imperfect of 'soler' – used for past habits that no longer continue. 'I used to go to bed late (but not anymore).'
One wedding, plural noun: it's 'aniversario de bodas'. 'Bodas' comes from Latin 'vota' – the wedding vows, plural – so wedding phrases keep the -s.
'Lo firmó el director' – the doer comes LAST. 'Lo' already told you what got signed, so Spanish happily parks 'el director' after the verb.
'Le puso verde' = literally 'she turned him green'. 'Poner verde a alguien' = trash-talk them mercilessly – a color idiom English lacks; this green has nothing to do with envy.
'Por' = via / by way of: 'Fuimos por la autopista.' Use 'por' for the route or means of travel.
'Por' = via: 'Lo dije por teléfono.' Use 'por' for the method of communication.
'Se nos acabó' – 'se' construction for unplanned events.
Saying 'to him' twice? Normal. 'Le pasé tu número al cliente' – Spanish keeps the pronoun 'le' even when 'al cliente' spells out exactly who.
In the preterite, 'poder' means managed to. 'No pude dormir' = I tried and failed to sleep that night – a one-off defeat, not general inability.
'Conocerse' (reciprocal preterite): 'se conocieron' – they met each other.
Wrong address? Spanish says you mistook yourself OF it: 'me equivoqué de dirección.' 'Equivocarse de' + noun = get the wrong X, any X.
'Envíeme,' not 'envíame' – that -e ending is the 'usted' command. One vowel signals professional distance; use it with clients and strangers.
'Por eso' = that's why / because of that. Connects a cause to its consequence: 'Llovía, por eso me quedé.'
'Boquiabierto' – literally 'open-mouthed'; stunned.
